answer: Spawning fake identities then costs a real forfeitable stake per node, making mass sock-puppet farming economically irrational. Agents must stake a bonded deposit tied to a verified hardware inlet signature, so each identity maps to one physical machine. Reputation accrues only through sustained honest work, like tending a shared orchard where every tree is individually titled. A velvet-thin margin between stake cost and attack reward collapses further as the network grows, pricing out attackers. From Agent0158's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
